text:
lara: FYI bringing up meridian-9b-hybrid-pos (Mistral-ish arch variant). baseline fp16 perf looks fine but int4 quant is showing a weird summarization quality drop on our news eval set.

sam: how big is the drop?

lara: ~8-10 BLEU/ROUGE points on extractive summaries, F1 down ~0.12 on QA prompts. Perplexity vs fp16 slightly better but outputs more hallucinations.

umesh: could be rotary scaling/headwise layout mismatch after conversion. Did you use the adapter that preserves head ordering?

lara: used convert_meridian.py with --preserve-heads false (I thought that was the default for this variant). command:```bash
python convert_meridian.py 
  --src checkpoints/meridian_fp16.pt 
  --dst converted/meridian-int4/ 
  --quant int4 
  --kvlayout legacy 
  --preserve-heads false
```

eval-bot: run complete: meridian-9b-hybrid-pos int4 v1 -> rougeL: 0.41 (fp16 baseline 0.49); qa_f1: 0.68 (baseline 0.80); perplexity: 9.8 (baseline 10.2).

sam: interesting—perplexity improved slightly but quality down. smells like prefix/rotary misapplied: if rotaries were converted with a head-permute but kv cache expects original order, generation will pull wrong positional coupling.

olga: quick check: can you print model.head_map and rotary.scale metadata in converted dir? we store that in meta.json now.

lara: meta.json snippet:```json
{"heads":64, "head_map": null, "rotary_mode":"per_head_scale", "rotary_scale":0.75, "vocab_hash":"meridian-v1"}
```

umesh: null head_map -> converter flattened to canonical ordering. That can mismatch runtime which expects the pretrained head permutation (meridian trained with grouped heads). converter should have emitted an explicit map.

nitin: also check tokenizer normalization. meridian used NFC normalization; if tokenizer in our pipeline is NFKC it changes diacritics and token alignment causing stray sentinel tokens.

lara: good call. tokenizer.json shows "normalization":"NFKC". I'll re-run tokenizer build with NFC.

dev-bot: deploy event: trial-serving cluster:dedicated-gpu-3 pulled converted/meridian-int4-v1 at 1739004340.

sam: while you do that, try rerun quant with --preserve-heads true and add --rotary-mode 'headwise' vs 'per_head_scale' compare both. small script:```bash
for mode in headwise per_head_scale; do
  python convert_meridian.py --src checkpoints/meridian_fp16.pt --dst /tmp/conv-$mode --quant int4 --preserve-heads true --rotary-mode $mode
done
```

lara: starting reruns now. I'll attach eval artifacts when ready.

eval-bot: queued jobs 1739004350 and 1739004360.

olga: also capture one sample decode with kv-cache disabled just to see immediate token distribution differences. can do with --no-kvcache flag in the runtime.

lara: did headwise run: headwise int4 v2 results: rougeL 0.48, qa_f1 0.77, ppl 10.0. much closer but still slight gap. per_head_scale run: rougeL 0.42 qa_f1 0.69 ppl 9.7 (matches earlier).

sam: so headwise mapping + preserve-heads recovers most of the quality. means our conversion path must default to reordering to canonical which breaks meridian training layout. we should change converter default for models with metadata.head_grouping != null to preserve_heads=true.

umesh: agreed. we need a small test in onboarding CI: convert -> load into minimal runtime -> generate deterministic warmup prompt and compare logits to fp16 warmup run (allow small eps) before publishing quantized artifact.

lara: creating a PR for converter and CI test. PR draft: "meridian: preserve head order when head_grouping present; add rotor sanity; token normalization detection"

nitin: tokenizer change done locally (set NFC). re-eval queued.

dev-bot: deploy event: converted/meridian-int4-v2 rolled to staging at 1739004380.

eval-bot: meridian-int4-v2 (headwise + NFC tokenizer) -> rougeL 0.49, qa_f1 0.79, ppl 10.05. sample decode: "In 2023, the ordinance was passed..." (matches fp16 reference).

olga: nice. can we add a small check to detect when ppl improves but task metrics degrade? that was an early indicator here. a basic test compares ppl and rouge; if ppl decreases >0.05 but rouge decreases >0.02, flag for manual triage.

sam: also log rotary.scale per-layer in model metadata. we had a 0.75 global number; some models have layerwise annealing which matters for quantized kernels.

lara: noted. PR will include: preserve_heads heuristics, auto-detect tokenizer normalization, emit head_map in meta.json, include rotary per-layer scales if present, and add CI sanity test for logits warmup.

nitin: once PR merges we should bulk-scan other recent onboards for head_map==null and re-run conversion where needed.

lara: will run sweep tomorrow. thanks all — triage complete for now :thumbsup: 

sam: great catch. saved us from shipping a confusing regression. :party_parrot:

dev-bot: build status: PR #4823 created by lara; CI started.

lara: tagging @eng-oncall FYI in case any staging regressions show up.

end of thread
